questions.question: When constructing a supervised fine‑tuning (SFT) dataset for chat models, which practice best preserves alignment between training and inference time behavior?
questions.choice_A: Use the exact chat template that will be used at inference, including special tokens and role tags, and mask loss on user/system turns
questions.choice_B: Strip all special tokens to simplify tokenization and compute loss on all tokens presented
questions.choice_C: Concatenate all dialog messages without delimiters to maximize sequence length utilization
questions.choice_D: Randomize the order of messages within a dialog to increase data diversity

questions.question: In pairwise preference datasets for reward modeling or DPO‑style training, which pairing principle is most important to avoid label leakage and preserve learning signal?
questions.choice_A: Ensuring the rejected answer is always from a different model checkpoint than the chosen answer
questions.choice_B: Ensuring the chosen and rejected completions respond to the same prompt and differ primarily in qualities the objective cares about
questions.choice_C: Ensuring the chosen completion is longer than the rejected one to increase token coverage
questions.choice_D: Ensuring the pairs are sampled uniformly across all prompt categories regardless of difficulty

questions.question: Which batching strategy most effectively reduces padding waste for mixed‑length sequences while maintaining high GPU utilization?
questions.choice_A: Randomly shuffle examples and use a fixed global batch size
questions.choice_B: Pad all sequences to the maximum context window supported by the model
questions.choice_C: Bucket sequences by similar lengths and form batches within buckets, optionally with packing
questions.choice_D: Sort all sequences by length and use a single giant batch per step

questions.question: When using sequence packing (concatenating multiple examples into one long sequence with separators), which additional implementation detail is critical to avoid cross‑example leakage?
questions.choice_A: Using a higher learning rate for packed batches
questions.choice_B: Applying label smoothing to reduce overfitting
questions.choice_C: Dropping the last incomplete pack each epoch
questions.choice_D: Resetting attention via proper segment boundaries or attention masks so tokens cannot attend across example boundaries

questions.question: Compared to training purely on an offline dataset, sampling model outputs on‑policy during preference optimization primarily addresses which risk?
questions.choice_A: Distribution shift between the model’s evolving policy and the fixed data, which can make gradients stale or biased
questions.choice_B: Excessive compute cost from decoding steps
questions.choice_C: Overfitting to prompts seen during pretraining
questions.choice_D: Instability from mixed precision arithmetic

questions.question: In RLHF with a KL penalty, how is sequence‑level KL most commonly computed in practice?
questions.choice_A: By measuring the cosine distance between hidden states of the policy and reference models
questions.choice_B: By summing the token‑level KL divergence between policy and reference log‑probabilities over the generated tokens, optionally normalized by sequence length
questions.choice_C: By comparing the temperatures used during sampling
questions.choice_D: By counting the number of repeated n‑grams in the output

questions.question: Which hyperparameter setup most directly controls the effective batch size in distributed SFT?
questions.choice_A: Number of data loader workers times the number of GPUs
questions.choice_B: LoRA rank times the microbatch size
questions.choice_C: Microbatch size × gradient accumulation steps × number of data‑parallel replicas
questions.choice_D: Sequence length × learning rate warmup steps

questions.question: Which is a key reproducibility pitfall specific to large‑scale distributed training?
questions.choice_A: Using the same tokenizer version across machines
questions.choice_B: Saving optimizer state with the model checkpoint
questions.choice_C: Fixing random seeds for data order and dropout
questions.choice_D: Non‑deterministic communication and kernel choices across devices, causing run‑to‑run variability even with fixed seeds

questions.question: When logging training for preference optimization, what should you track to diagnose mode collapse toward the reference model?
questions.choice_A: Sequence‑level KL to the reference over time and its correlation with reward
questions.choice_B: Only the training loss averaged over the entire dataset
questions.choice_C: Number of unique prompts seen per epoch
questions.choice_D: Wall‑clock time per step

questions.question: What is a practical compute/memory tradeoff when increasing context length during SFT?
questions.choice_A: Memory decreases because longer sequences reduce padding
questions.choice_B: Compute and memory scale roughly as $O(n^2)$ with sequence length for standard attention, motivating techniques like gradient checkpointing and flash attention
questions.choice_C: Compute scales linearly with sequence length while memory stays constant
questions.choice_D: Longer sequences always improve validation loss regardless of batch size

questions.question: Why is it important to mask loss on user and system tokens in chat SFT?
questions.choice_A: To prevent the model from learning the tokenizer’s vocabulary distribution
questions.choice_B: To enforce that the model only conditions on its own outputs
questions.choice_C: To train the model to predict only assistant turns while using user/system turns as context, matching inference‑time usage
questions.choice_D: To stabilize mixed precision training by reducing gradient variance

questions.question: Which statement best captures the difference between DDP, ZeRO/FSDP, and tensor/pipeline parallelism?
questions.choice_A: DDP shards activations while ZeRO shards gradients; tensor parallelism only affects the data loader
questions.choice_B: DDP replicates full parameters per rank; ZeRO/FSDP shard optimizer state, gradients, and optionally parameters; tensor/pipeline parallelism split model computation within a layer or across layers
questions.choice_C: ZeRO is only for CPUs, while DDP is only for GPUs
questions.choice_D: Pipeline parallelism is incompatible with mixed precision

questions.question: What data hygiene step is crucial when building preference datasets from web‑scale sources to avoid evaluation contamination?
questions.choice_A: Applying nucleus sampling during data collection
questions.choice_B: Decontaminating against evaluation and test sets using n‑gram overlap or hashing, and deduplicating near‑duplicates
questions.choice_C: Sorting prompts by length before labeling
questions.choice_D: Removing all punctuation from prompts and completions

questions.question: Which setting most often improves numerical stability without significant loss of model quality in large‑scale LLM finetuning?
questions.choice_A: Training in float32 throughout
questions.choice_B: Using bfloat16 for compute with gradient clipping and an appropriate loss scaler (if needed)
questions.choice_C: Turning off gradient clipping to avoid clipping bias
questions.choice_D: Using extremely small learning rates with no warmup

questions.question: When sampling during training (on‑policy), which control most directly balances exploration and training signal quality for preference optimization?
questions.choice_A: Batch size
questions.choice_B: Weight decay
questions.choice_C: Sampling temperature/top‑p combined with per‑prompt sampling budget and rejection filtering
questions.choice_D: Sequence packing size

questions.question: What should be saved in checkpoints to enable exact resumption and reproducibility across distributed runs?
questions.choice_A: Only model weights and tokenizer files
questions.choice_B: Model weights, but allow the optimizer to reinitialize for faster restart
questions.choice_C: Model/optimizer/scheduler states plus global and per‑device RNG states, data sampler state, and configuration hashes
questions.choice_D: Only experiment logs because they contain hyperparameters

questions.question: How does gradient accumulation help with limited GPU memory budgets?
questions.choice_A: It reduces parameter count by pruning layers during training
questions.choice_B: It allows smaller microbatches to be processed sequentially and their gradients accumulated to emulate a larger effective batch size
questions.choice_C: It compresses optimizer states to 8‑bit during backpropagation
questions.choice_D: It offloads activations to disk to free GPU memory

questions.question: In preference optimization with a KL penalty, what happens if the KL coefficient is set too low?
questions.choice_A: The model collapses to copying the reference distribution
questions.choice_B: Training becomes strictly more stable
questions.choice_C: The policy may exploit the reward model, drifting far from the reference and harming generalization or safety
questions.choice_D: Gradients vanish because the KL dominates the loss

questions.question: Which logging practice most helps compare runs across changing code and data versions?
questions.choice_A: Recording only the git commit of the training script
questions.choice_B: Logging dataset version identifiers or content hashes, tokenizer version, full hyperparameter configs, and environment metadata
questions.choice_C: Using filenames that include the learning rate
questions.choice_D: Relying on default TensorBoard scalars

questions.question: Which engineering detail most affects throughput in multi‑node DDP training on large models?
questions.choice_A: Using Adam instead of SGD
questions.choice_B: NCCL backend configuration and network bandwidth for all‑reduce operations; using gradient bucketing and overlap of compute/communication
questions.choice_C: Doubling the logging frequency
questions.choice_D: Turning off activation checkpointing

questions.question: Why might offline preference datasets still be useful even if on‑policy sampling is possible?
questions.choice_A: They guarantee no distribution shift
questions.choice_B: They are cheaper and faster to train on, provide stable baselines, and can bootstrap initial policies or reward models before on‑policy fine‑tuning
questions.choice_C: They eliminate the need for a reference model
questions.choice_D: They remove the need for KL regularization entirely
